messages:
maya: Starting the design review for the routing policies editor tomorrow 10am PT. Focus: preview interactions, validation copy, and reorder UX.

chris: can we add a quick demo of the preview sim? I think folks still expect live token-by-token preview vs snapshot. :eyes:

sam: live previews are expensive, maybe demo with a 'playback' that steps through decisions and highlights the fired rule. shows rule highlights and matched conditions.

aleks: +1. Also want a clearer affordance for manual reordering — drag handles look tiny on mobile and feel fiddly on hover-only interactions.

leo: accessibility note: drag handles need 44px target or explicit keyboard controls. Suggested: add up/down buttons with aria-live announcing position change ("Rule moved to position 3").

chris: mockup update: added visible up/down buttons next to each rule. Also changed focus outline to #005fcc to meet 3:1 contrast for the theme.

maya: copy tweak proposal: current validation bubble says "Invalid" — make it actionable, e.g. "Rule invalid: missing match condition — add a condition or disable this rule". Short and prescriptive.

sam: good, will wire that into the validations reducer. Proposed shape for the API error object in the UI:
```json
{
  "error": "missing_match",
  "message": "Rule invalid: add at least one match condition to activate this rule",
  "severity": "error"
}
```

aleks: Simulation UX: show which rule fired in the preview, and allow stepping through priority order. maybe a small timeline bar with ticks for each rule evaluation.

chris: thinking: preview modal header should read "Simulation — input text" and below a stepper with compact rule chips. clicking a chip highlights that rule in the canvas and shows matched fields.

leo: ensure the stepper is keyboard operable: left/right arrows or buttons, and screen reader reads "Step 2 of 4: Matched rule: route to dedicated". Also, ensure color isn't the only indicator — add an icon or underline.

maya: decision checklist for the meeting: 1) adopt up/down buttons + drag handles; 2) update validation copy to actionable text; 3) simulation stepper with rule highlighting and matched fields; 4) keyboard + screen reader a11y acceptance criteria. anyone object?

sam: no objections. I'll slot a frontend spike for next sprint to prototype the stepper and buttons.

chris: I'll update the Figma screens and add annotations for a11y behavior. link will be posted before the review. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Reminder — design-review event scheduled at 2026-03-24 17:00 UTC.

maya: thanks everyone — I'll circulate meeting notes + updated mockups after the sync.
